title: Soccer Manager
tagline: A full-stack team management platform built to help soccer coaches and team managers organize their teams, track player stats, and communicate with players and parents.

title: Calculator
tagline: A fully responsive calculator built from scratch with vanilla JavaScript.
overview: A browser-based calculator supporting standard arithmetic operations, built to strengthen my grasp of DOM manipulation, event handling, and operator precedence logic without relying on any frameworks or libraries.
approach: Structured the UI with semantic HTML and a CSS grid layout for consistent button alignment across screen sizes.
Implemented an operator-precedence-aware calculation engine in vanilla JavaScript, handling chained operations and edge cases like divide-by-zero.
Containerized the app with Docker and deployed it to Fly.io for a lightweight, reproducible hosting setup.
results: Solidified my understanding of state management and event delegation without a framework.
First project I shipped with a full Docker-based deployment pipeline.

title: Number Guessing Game
tagline: An interactive number guessing game with real-time feedback and hint logic.
overview: A browser game where the player guesses a randomly generated number, built to practice working with game state, user feedback loops, and conditional logic in JavaScript.
approach: Designed the game loop around a simple state machine tracking attempts, guess history, and win/lose conditions.
Added dynamic higher/lower feedback that updates the DOM in real time as the player guesses.
Deployed via Fly.io to keep the project accessible as a live demo for anyone reviewing my work.
results: Reinforced core JavaScript fundamentals: conditionals, loops, and DOM updates driven by state changes.

title: Weather App
tagline: A weather lookup app that fetches and displays live forecast data from a public API.
overview: A weather app that lets users search any city and see current conditions, built to practice working with asynchronous JavaScript and third-party APIs.
approach: Integrated a public weather API using fetch and async/await, with error handling for invalid city names and failed requests.
Built a responsive UI that maps weather conditions to icons and dynamic background styling.
Deployed the app to Fly.io for a live, shareable demo.
results: First project where I worked directly with an external REST API and handled real-world async edge cases like rate limits, bad input, and network failures.

title: School Website
tagline: A multi-page informational website built for a school project brief.
overview: A static, multi-page website designed and built to a course brief, focused on clean semantic structure, responsive layout, and accessible navigation.
approach: Planned the site's information architecture and page hierarchy before writing any code.
Built fully responsive layouts with CSS Flexbox/Grid, tested across breakpoints.
Focused on semantic HTML for accessibility and maintainability.
results: One of my earliest projects, and a good marker of how far my HTML/CSS fundamentals have come since.
